title: Spring Boot Basics and REST Controllers
description: What Spring Boot adds to Spring, generating and reading a Boot project, dependency injection and bean scopes, how auto-configuration works, and REST controllers with path, query and body parameters, ResponseEntity status codes and an OpenAPI description explored in Swagger UI.
sourceCoverageNotes: Course slice: Standard S1-S13 and Fast FT1-FT8. This module covers Standard S1-S2.
Module grouping is a second-mate grouping decision (closing source-gap-spring-boot-modules), not syllabus: modules follow calendar day sequence, S1-S2 here.

Module coding lab: required Standard real-toolchain practice at coding-lab/ with at least one tested task for each of the nine taught topics (trackRequirement standard required, fast not-required), mvn -q -o test, Spring Boot 4.1.2, no database, no container engine; Fast skips coding labs.

Standard placement: the required module coding lab follows reading-an-openapi-spec-and-exploring-it-in-swagger-ui, the module's final taught topic (S2, fourth of four), and closes the module before porting-and-configuration starts on S3. Timing is an authoring estimate, not piloted, and is NOT a proven fit: the four S2 pages are 58 minutes, the lab tasks are 36 minutes and the one-time online setup (mvn -q dependency:go-offline) is about 8 minutes, so the required work totals about 102 minutes (58 + 36 + 8) against 95 minutes available (the four S2 page blocks plus the Concept-day 40-minute coding-lab block). The schedule decision is open. The lab sits outside the calendar's lab overlay (S2 is a Concept day with requiredLab false).

Partial objective coverage in the module coding lab (recorded): every taught topic has at least one tested task, and some objectives are only partly exercised. beans-and-bean-scopes#o1 is practised in Task 1 (register the catalog bean with a @Bean method in a @Configuration class); scope objectives o2 and o3 stay on the page. dependency-injection-replacing-manual-wiring#o1 is practised as constructor injection of one registered bean into the controller; wiring across controller, service and repository layers is taught by constructor-injection-across-layers and applied in the porting-and-configuration module lab on S3-S4. response-codes-with-responseentity#o1 is practised for 200, 201 with Location and 404 but not 204, which the page's editor activity covers. spring-vs-spring-boot-what-boot-adds#o2 is practised by Task 7 (the embedded server started from main); the BOM-managed parent and starter appear in the shipped pom without a dedicated check. generating-a-spring-boot-project-and-its-structure#o2 is practised by Task 4, which checks that application.properties is built from src/main/resources with two settings. how-auto-configuration-works#o1 is practised by Task 5 (component scanning across two packages); the condition objectives stay on the page. reading-an-openapi-spec-and-exploring-it-in-swagger-ui#o1 is practised by Task 6 (one GET operation from a shipped OpenAPI document); springdoc and Swagger UI (o2, o3) stay on the page. Task 6 also checks the 400 for a missing and for a non-numeric required query parameter (path-query-and-body-parameters#o1 and #o2).
